text: Nine claims for Zirconia Crown Restoration at Meridian Dental Institute are near-identical copies of one claim package: the same nine line items, narratives matching to within six bits on a 64-bit fingerprint - most of them byte-identical - and amounts confined to a 3.8% band around $1,300. The nine claims were filed for nine different patients billed to six different insurers, and the patients share two submission devices between them; unrelated medical tourists do not file paperwork from the same office computers. Any single element has an innocent reading - dental crowns are standardized packages and clinics do reuse wording - but standardization does not spread one narrative across six insurers from two shared machines, with every claim arranged by the same broker. This is the claim-mill signature: one perfected package resubmitted with the names swapped. An honest alternative worth ruling out is a franchise billing system that stamps identical templates across genuinely separate treatments. Next step: request the underlying treatment records for two claims in the cluster and compare radiographs and lab work orders line by line - a mill cannot produce nine distinct sets.
